summary.en: Supports roots and marks the exposed habitat.
summary.zh: 承托树根，标出露泥的生境。

detail.en:
The mud bank gives this teaching scene a surface, with a lower channel along the front. Tide poses change which surfaces appear covered. [S27, S30]

This is an independent habitat model. Its outline, dimensions and drawn numbers are design choices, not a survey of Sungei Buloh. [S30]
detail.zh:
泥岸承托这幅教学场景，前缘有较低的潮沟；潮位姿态改变画面上被水覆盖的区域。[S27, S30]

这是独立的生境模型；轮廓、尺寸和画出的数量都属于设计，不是双溪布洛测量结果。[S30]

summary.en: Shows low and high water as two schematic poses.
summary.zh: 以两种示意姿态显示低潮和高潮。

detail.en:
Incoming tide changes the physical conditions around the mud bank. The water surface moves between two illustrative positions. [S27, S30]

These are not tide heights, a tide prediction or a water-volume calculation. The food graph uses the same links in both poses. [S30]
detail.zh:
潮水涨落改变泥岸周围的条件；这里的水面只在两个示意位置间移动。[S27, S30]

这些位置不是实测潮高或潮汐预报，也不计算水量；两种姿态使用相同的食物关系。[S30]

summary.en: Marks a refuge used by fiddler crabs.
summary.zh: 标示招潮蟹可躲藏的洞口。

detail.en:
Fiddler crabs retreat into burrows during high tide. The opening remains visible as a separate habitat feature. [S5]

This short opening does not reconstruct the shape, depth or air supply of a real burrow. [S30]
detail.zh:
招潮蟹在高潮时会退入洞中；洞口是独立的生境结构，即使蟹隐藏也仍然保留。[S5]

这里只显示一个短洞口，没有重建真实洞穴的形状、深度或供气情况。[S30]

summary.en: Leaves make food and can excrete salt.
summary.zh: 叶片制造食物，并能排出盐分。

detail.en:
Api-api Putih (Avicennia alba) has leaves with salt glands. This salt-handling feature belongs to this named plant, not every mangrove. [S3]

Its shallow lateral roots connect to upright pencil-shaped breathing roots. The neighbouring Bakau is a separate tree. [S2, S3]
detail.zh:
Api-api Putih（Avicennia alba）的叶片有盐腺；这种排盐方式属于这株具名植物，不能推广到所有红树。[S3]

它的浅侧根与直立的铅笔状呼吸根相连；旁边的 Bakau 是另一株独立的树。[S2, S3]

summary.en: Connects the tree to its breathing roots.
summary.zh: 把树体与呼吸根连接起来。

detail.en:
Avicennia alba develops shallow lateral roots below the muddy surface. Upright breathing roots arise from this connected system. [S3]

The cutaway exposes the connection; the spacing and thickness here are schematic. [S30]
detail.zh:
Avicennia alba 的浅侧根在泥面下延伸；直立的呼吸根从这套相连的根系长出。[S3]

剖切让连接关系显露出来；这里的间距和粗细都是示意。[S30]

summary.en: Protrudes above mud to help gas exchange.
summary.zh: 伸出泥面，帮助气体交换。

detail.en:
Pencil-shaped breathing roots protrude vertically from the shallow lateral root system and take in oxygen. [S2, S3]

Every upright root in this model joins a lateral branch below the mud. The drawn heights are design values. [S30]
detail.zh:
铅笔状呼吸根从浅侧根系统直立伸出泥面，吸收氧气。[S2, S3]

模型中的每根直立根都在泥下接上侧根；画出的高度属于设计值。[S30]

summary.en: Makes food and supplies leaf material.
summary.zh: 制造食物，并提供叶片物质。

detail.en:
This separate Bakau Minyak tree has prop roots descending from its trunk. Mangrove trees provide shelter and a supply of leaf material. [S2, S6, S8]

The food-web node represents continuing leaf supply. Removing that node does not make old fallen leaves disappear. [S30]
detail.zh:
这株独立的 Bakau Minyak 有从树干向下延伸的支柱根；红树提供庇护和叶片物质。[S2, S6, S8]

食物网节点表示持续的叶片供应；移走这个节点不会使已有落叶马上消失。[S30]

summary.en: Anchors the tree and offers shelter.
summary.zh: 支撑树体，并提供庇护。

detail.en:
Bakau prop roots extend from the trunk towards the mud and anchor the tree. Root spaces also shelter young animals. [S2]

These roots belong to the Bakau, separate from the neighbouring Api-api pencil roots. [S30]
detail.zh:
Bakau 的支柱根从树干向泥地延伸，支撑树体；根之间的空间也能为幼小动物提供庇护。[S2]

这套根属于 Bakau，与邻株 Api-api 的铅笔状根分开。[S30]

summary.en: Supplies organic material to feeding pathways.
summary.zh: 给取食路径提供有机物质。

detail.en:
Some mangrove crabs eat fallen leaves and fragment them into smaller pieces. Dead leaf material still contains food energy. [S6, S24]

Existing leaves stay visible when continuing tree supply is removed. Their disappearance and decomposition rate are not simulated. [S30]
detail.zh:
有些红树林蟹取食落叶，把叶片弄成较小的碎片；死去的叶片仍含食物中的能量。[S6, S24]

关闭树木持续供应时，已有落叶仍保留在画面里；这里没有模拟它们消失或分解的速率。[S30]

summary.en: Makes food using sunlight.
summary.zh: 利用阳光制造食物。

detail.en:
Algae are producers in these selected pathways. Some fiddlers and tree-climbing crabs consume algae, with evidence from different observations. [S7, S18, S24]

This patch marks a functional group on the surface; it is not a giant visible single cell or a measured local algal cover. [S30]
detail.zh:
藻类是这些选入路径中的生产者；一些招潮蟹和树蟹会取食藻类，证据来自不同的观察。[S7, S18, S24]

这个斑块标示泥面的功能组，不是一颗肉眼可见的巨大细胞，也不是当地藻类覆盖率测量。[S30]

summary.en: Small claw feeds; the enlarged male claw displays.
summary.zh: 小螯取食，雄蟹的大螯用于展示。

detail.en:
A male fiddler has one enlarged claw and a smaller feeding claw, with eye stalks and four pairs of walking legs. [S5, S32]

The group node is represented by one specimen symbol. High tide hides it in the burrow; drawing one does not report abundance. [S5, S30]
detail.zh:
雄招潮蟹有一只大螯和一只取食小螯，还有眼柄及四对步足。[S5, S32]

群组节点用一个标本符号表示；高潮时它藏进洞中。画一只不代表野外数量。[S5, S30]

summary.en: Eats leaf material and can climb above water.
summary.zh: 取食叶片物质，也能爬到水面之上。

detail.en:
This teaching node groups several climbing crab kinds. Leaf material is supported by the Sungei Buloh report, while the separate algae input comes from an indexed account; these do not establish one Episesarma species diet. [S6, S7]

This specimen has four pairs of walking legs and two claws. The higher pose is schematic, with the feet against the Bakau trunk. [S32, S30]
detail.zh:
这个教学节点合并几类会攀爬的蟹。双溪布洛报道支持叶片取食，另一个索引资料支持藻类输入；这些资料没有证实同一种 Episesarma 同时具有这份食谱。[S6, S7]

这只示意标本有四对步足和一对螯；较高的姿态是示意，步足贴着 Bakau 树干。[S32, S30]

summary.en: Pectoral fins move this fish over exposed mud.
summary.zh: 胸鳍帮助这条鱼在露泥上移动。

detail.en:
Giant mudskippers are fish. Modified gill chambers and skin help gas exchange out of water; fleshy pectoral fins help movement. [S4]

General guides include crabs as food, while local diet samples differ. The selected links are possibilities, not a measured menu. [S4, S13, S31]
detail.zh:
弹涂鱼是鱼；特化的鳃腔和皮肤帮助它离水时进行气体交换，肉质胸鳍帮助移动。[S4]

一般指南把蟹列为其食物，但不同当地样本有差异；这些线表示可能关系，不是实测食谱。[S4, S13, S31]

summary.en: Long legs, neck and bill support feeding.
summary.zh: 长腿、长颈与长喙帮助取食。

detail.en:
Herons have long necks and bills and eat fish and crustaceans. NParks lists herons among predators of giant mudskippers. [S4, S29]

This two-legged specimen represents herons generally, not a verified local feeding event by one named heron species. [S30]
detail.zh:
鹭有长颈和长喙，会吃鱼和甲壳类；NParks 把鹭列为弹涂鱼的捕食者。[S4, S29]

这只两腿的标本泛指鹭类，不声称已核实某种鹭在当地发生了一次具体捕食事件。[S30]

summary.en: Shows prey outside the selected food graph.
summary.zh: 表示选入食物网之外的其他猎物。

detail.en:
Herons and giant mudskippers can eat small fish. Real organisms may have food options outside a short teaching graph. [S4, S29]

This generic fish has no solver link. Its presence reminds us that no shown path is not the same as no possible food in nature. [S30]
detail.zh:
鹭和弹涂鱼都可能吃小鱼；真实生物的食物选择可能超出简短教学图的范围。[S4, S29]

这条普通小鱼没有求解连线；它提醒我们，图内没有路径，不等于自然界没有可能的食物。[S30]

summary.en: Helps explain decomposition of leaf material.
summary.zh: 帮助说明叶片物质的分解。

detail.en:
Bacteria help break down mangrove leaf litter. They obtain energy from organic material in decomposition. [S10]

These separate enlarged shapes are schematic and not to scale. They are not giant bacteria living above the mud surface. [S30]
detail.zh:
细菌参与红树林落叶的分解；它们在分解过程中从有机物质获得能量。[S10]

旁置的放大形状是示意，不按比例；这不是生活在泥面上的巨大细菌。[S30]

summary.en: Breaks down dead organic material.
summary.zh: 分解死亡的有机物质。

detail.en:
Fungi are among the organisms that break down mangrove leaf litter. They obtain energy from organic material, not from photosynthesis. [S10]

The branching threads are an enlarged schematic, not a species identification or a measured microscopic view. [S30]
detail.zh:
真菌是参与红树林落叶分解的生物之一；它们从有机物质获得能量，不进行光合作用来制造食物。[S10]

分枝丝体是放大示意，不是物种鉴定，也不是实测显微图像。[S30]

summary.en: Marks a water-retaining gill chamber.
summary.zh: 标示能保水的鳃腔。

detail.en:
The giant mudskipper has modified gill chambers that support breathing out of water, alongside skin gas exchange. It remains a fish. [S4]

This open cavity is an explanatory schematic, not a verified anatomical section or a lung. No detailed gill anatomy is claimed. [S30]
detail.zh:
弹涂鱼的特化鳃腔与皮肤气体交换，帮助它离水时呼吸；它仍然是鱼。[S4]

这个开放空腔只是解释示意，不是经核实的解剖断面，也不是肺；这里没有声称显示详细鳃部结构。[S30]

summary.en: Marks the far observation edge.
summary.zh: 标示远侧的观察边界。

detail.en: A simple boardwalk edge suggests observing the habitat without collecting animals. It is scenery with no geographic claim. [S30]
detail.zh: 简洁的步道边缘提示在栖地外观察；这是场景件，没有地理含义。[S30]

summary.en: Supports the habitat and separate schematic insets.
summary.zh: 承托生境和旁置的示意近景。

detail.en: This base holds the habitat and the separate enlarged schematics. It is a display stand with no geographic meaning. [S30]
detail.zh: 底座承托生境与旁置的放大示意，是没有地理含义的展示台。[S30]

name.zh: 示意近景 · 不按比例

note.en: Fallen leaf material, not a living producer node for detritus.
note.zh: 这条边表示叶片输入，不把死叶当活生产者。

note.en: Indexed climbing-crab account. This selected group-level possibility is not a verified local Episesarma diet link. Different climbing-crab kinds are grouped here.
note.zh: 只读到攀爬蟹类资料的索引。此线是功能组层面的可能关系，不是本地某种 Episesarma 的已核食谱；这里合并了不同蟹类。

note.en: Observed elsewhere; possible food-group link, not a Singapore measurement.
note.zh: 外地观察支持可能关系；不是本地食性实测。

note.en: General guide differs from the Lim Chu Kang sample; not a measured local pair.
note.zh: 一般指南与林厝港样本不同；不是本地实测配对。

note.en: The indexed paper reports opportunistic feeding on an Episesarma crab, without a feeding frequency. This functional group includes other climbing crabs.
note.zh: 论文索引报告了对 Episesarma 蟹的机会取食观察，没有取食频率。这个功能组也包含其他攀爬蟹类。

note.en: NParks identifies herons as predators of giant mudskippers.
note.zh: NParks 明述鹭会捕食这种弹涂鱼。

note.en: Selected possible feeding links. Missing pathways do not predict extinction.
note.zh: 这里只选入一些可能的取食关系。路径中断不等于预测灭绝。
